endorsements.quote: Phased deployment models may be a solution with gradual integration of DT components starting from high-impact workflow segments (e.g., specimen tracking or quality control monitoring), with scalability toward full-system modeling over time [ 27 ].

To address this, targeted staff training modules and continuous professional development programs can improve user acceptance and ensure that technical personnel are equipped with the necessary skills to engage with DT systems effectively [ 28 ].
Solutions should include robust data governance frameworks, with clear protocols for anonymization, access control, and compliance with standards such as GDPR or HIPAA [ 30 ].

unlisted_practices: Involve key stakeholders early in the design and testing phases of digital twin implementation to enhance buy-in and reduce resistance.
Use edge computing or hybrid cloud architectures to keep critical processing on-premises and reduce data exposure.
Integrate digital twin functionality within existing Laboratory Information Systems rather than requiring complete infrastructure overhaul.
Conduct longitudinal studies evaluating the long-term clinical and economic outcomes of digital twins in pathology laboratories.
Research the ethical implications of AI-driven diagnostics in pathology.
